facts.fact: The Ministry of Health's plan states that the HMIS is governed by the directors of the ministry's HMER Unit, that its HIS Unit is the national repository of all health data, and that service data are held in a single DHIS2 database; no date is given, so the publication date is used.

The Ministry of Health issued a five-year Data Quality Improvement Plan for the HMIS in June 2022, running 2022 to 2026, costed at US$7,312,887.50 in its activity table (US$7.3 million in the summary, with year one at US$2.2 million), and budgeting DHIS2 training, a DHIS2 operating procedure and computers for data officers; it says the HIS and ICT Strategic Plan before it covered 2016 to 2021.

The Ministry of Health's plan names donor dependency as a threat, reports no budget line for HMER in the public budget and no ministry counterpart funding, donor reliance for buying and maintaining data equipment, and data staff off the government payroll; it lists advocacy for a specific HIS budget line as an activity. No date is given, so the publication date is used.

The plan describes facilities compiling monthly paper reporting forms from ledgers and tally sheets, which districts and counties collect, with data clerks using DHIS2; its computers (153 laptops), modems and internet subscriptions go to national, county and district data officers (15 counties, 93 districts), none to facilities. It does not say in terms at which office the forms are keyed; the publication date is used.

The plan gives no figure for facilities entering their own reports; it reports from the ministry's HIS system assessment (243 facilities, reporting period April to June 2020) that 70.4% of health facilities lacked a computer, tablet or internet, and sets a 2021 baseline of 28.6% of facilities with internet and a computer against a 2026 target of 75%.

The plan treats the patient record as a paper chart: it reports patient charts stocked out since 2016, 51.9% of facilities short of shelves, tables and boxes for patient records, and budgets US$1,789,061.50 to supply standardized patient charts to all facilities; it names no electronic patient record, though it does not state that none exists. The publication date is used.

note: No tiers fact: the plan says the HMIS runs in public and private facilities countrywide without naming facility tiers. It publishes reporting completeness (95% against a 2016-2021 target of 100%; 2021 baseline 88.4% for public facilities) and timeliness (84.2%; baseline 80%), which no aspect carries. The summary's five-year cost (US$7.3 million) and the costing paragraph's (US$7,118,087.5) differ from the table's grand total. eDEWS and DSIS appear only in the acronym list.
